main_text.head: MASSYLI MEDITERRANEI qui & Masæsyli Africæ generaliter dictæ populi excipiunt Barccæ regionem ad æquatorem pergentibus.
main_text.p: Virgil. Aeneid.lib.4. Idem Aeneid.lib.4. Massyli diuini.MAssylique ruunt equites, & odora canum vis. Hinc mihi Massyla gentis monstrata sacerdos, Hesperidum templi custos, epulasque draconi Quæ dabat, & sacros seruabat in arbore ramos, Spargens humida mella, soporiferumque papauer. Hæc se carminibus promittit soluere mentes Quas velit, aft aliys duras immittere curas. Sistere aquam fluuijs, & vertere sidera retro: Noctumosque ciet manes. mugire videbis Sub pedibus terram, & descendere montibus ornos.
main_text.head: NVMIDÆ SEV NOMADES populi mediterranei vlteriores Massylis, si quis ad æquatorem pergat.
main_text.p: — quos Circinus vrit Æthiopas, primoque Indos sub Sole iacentes: Gætulos, Nomadasque agiles, Cilicasque rapaces. Palin.in Leone.Virgil.lib.3. Georg.Quid tibi pastores Libya, quid pascua versu Persequar? raris habitata mapalia tectis? Sæpe diem, noctemque, & totum ex ordine mensem Pascitur, itque pecus longa in deserta sine vllis Hospitijs: tantum campi iacet: omnia secum

page.notes: Dropped capital M of the first paragraph is read as "M"; the word "Massylique" is set with an italic initial. Several words in the verse are uncertain and are not marked individually; the lower-right "Armen-" is a catchword at the foot of the page. Page furniture and fleurons are not transcribed.
